prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a counter running diagonally across the lower foreground at about 0.4–0.8 m from the camera wearer, with an upright brown paper bag near the center (~0.4–0.6 m away), a payment terminal/monitor ~0.3 m further right and slightly behind the bag (~0.7–1.0 m away), a wire snack rack attached below the counter edge on the right in frames 1–2, and a person standing behind the counter to the left at roughly 0.8–1.2 m with their left hand resting on the counter surface (~0.5–0.7 m away). The person's torso faces toward the counter and camera wearer, though their head is cropped out of the top of the frame so gaze cannot be confirmed, while the counter, paper bag, snack rack, and the person's resting hand are all within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person. Across the 5 frames, the bright intensity on the paper bag and counter increases from frames 1–2 to frames 3–4 as the camera wearer leans in closer (~0.3–0.4 m from the bag) and turns slightly left before stepping back slightly and panning right in frame 5, where the bag partially occludes the background display case and terminal. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the continuous 3D surface gradient of the counter, the vertical relief of the paper bag, and the recessed depth of the wire rack immediately clear. However, the map is unreliable on the dark jacket and background doorway in frames 3–4, where low-reflectance clothing and glass/background regions collapse into uniform black holes that lose true metric separation.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only two foreground regions across the scene: the person behind the left side of the counter (about 0.8–1.2 m from the camera wearer, with their left hand extending onto the counter to ~0.5–0.7 m) and the flat laminated promotional mat ('PICK 5') lying on the counter surface (~0.4–0.7 m away, directly in front of the person's hand and to the left of the paper bag). In frames 1–4, the 'person' mask sits directly above and behind the 'book' mask (the misclassified promotional mat) with the person's hand touching the mat's upper edge within arm's reach of both people, while in frame 5 the mat is cropped out at the bottom-left and only the person's left arm and torso remain visible on the far left edge. Across frames 1 to 4, both masks shift rightward and expand in image area as the camera wearer moves closer and angles left toward the counter, before retreating to the left margin in frame 5 as the camera turns right. While the segmentation masks sharply delineate the boundary of the person's dark sleeve and hand against the cluttered counter and dark background in frames 1–5, the map is largely unreliable for full scene understanding. It mislabels the flat counter sign as a 'book', suffers from severe false-negative omissions by failing to segment the prominent brown paper bag, counter, monitor, and wire rack, and fragments the person's arm in frame 2.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a small magenta hand skeleton on the person's left hand resting on the counter (~0.6 m from the camera wearer) and a tiny, misplaced yellow body skeleton on the payment terminal (~0.8 m away, to the right of the paper bag) in frame 1, plus a single magenta hand skeleton at the bottom-left edge in frame 5 (~0.5 m away). From the RGB context, the person stands ~0.8–1.2 m away on the left side behind the counter facing toward the camera wearer with their head cropped out above the frame and their left hand within arm's reach of both the paper bag (~0.3 m to the right of the hand) and the camera wearer, while in frame 4 their right hand also enters on the far left holding a small object. Across the 5 frames, as the camera approaches and turns left in frames 3–4 and then turns back right in frame 5, the pose estimator completely loses track of the person's body and hands in frames 2, 3, and 4 before re-detecting only the left hand in frame 5. In frames 1 and 5, the magenta keypoints help localize the exact finger articulation of the person's left hand on the counter surface, which is small and partially motion-blurred in frame 5 of the RGB strip. However, the pose map is highly unreliable overall because heavy upper-body cropping at the top and left frame borders causes total misses of the person's torso and arms in every frame, and the payment terminal in frame 1 triggers a false-positive yellow body skeleton.
